title: Use the old EPP browser as the UI parity baseline
decision: The old EPP manual browser UI and layout should be treated as the target parity baseline for the standalone Archivist app, while replacing the generated static architecture with React and the local service.
context: The user was happy with the old UI and called out that Appendix A is not visible in the current scaffold. The old browser already contains the desired DOVAXIS header, grouped nav, document-first reader, metadata controls, and inline editing affordances.
rationale: The current scaffold proved service/workbook mechanics but regressed the browsing experience. Preserving the old visual and interaction baseline prevents the migration from accidentally losing the product surface the user already liked.
alternatives_considered: Continue evolving the current three-pane scaffold as the primary UI
Build workbook surfaces before restoring full document navigation
Use the generated HTML directly as the app
consequences: Appendix A must become visible through the normal full EPP document nav before deeper workbook polish is considered successful
React should port the old browser shell and interaction contracts rather than copy generated HTML
Documentation and parity prep should precede the next build slice
The seed workspace can remain a test fixture but should not define the user-facing EPP experience
